q: How does an AI chat assistant like ChatGPT produce its answers?
options: It looks up a single correct answer in a verified database
It predicts a helpful response based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text
A human expert reviews and approves each reply before it appears
It copies the most popular web page about your question
explain: Assistants run on large language models that predict responses from patterns in their training text, not from a verified answer database.

q: Which of these tasks is the strongest fit for an AI assistant without extra checking?
options: Finding today's exact train timings from Mumbai to Pune
Confirming the current repo rate for a loan decision
Getting the cut-off marks for a specific college this year
Turning a long school circular into five clear bullet points
explain: Summarising is about words and structure, where AI is strongest; current exact facts like timings, rates and cut-offs need checking.

q: Kavita asks an AI to 'write an email to my boss' and gets a generic reply. What is the most likely reason?
options: The AI only knows what she tells it, and she gave no context
Free versions of AI assistants cannot write work emails
She should have used a search engine instead of an assistant
The AI deliberately keeps first drafts generic to save time
explain: The AI is not a mind reader; without details like the boss's name, purpose and tone, it can only produce a generic email.

q: Ramesh wants to install ChatGPT on his phone. What should he check before installing an app?
options: That the app has the highest number of star ratings
That the app offers a paid unlock for faster answers
That the developer name matches the official company
That the app icon looks the same as the website logo
explain: Fake AI apps are common, so checking that the developer is the official company (such as OpenAI) protects you.

q: Which password practice does the course recommend for your AI account?
options: Reuse your UPI password so it is easy to remember
Share one password across the family's AI accounts
Use the same password as your email for convenience
Use a unique password not shared with banking or UPI
explain: A unique password, plus two-step verification on your email, keeps your AI account and financial accounts separately protected.

q: During setup, what does the course suggest doing with data, history and memory settings?
options: Read what each does and make a conscious choice about it
Switch every setting off because all of them are risky
Leave them at the defaults since they cannot be changed
Ignore them until you upgrade to a paid plan
explain: You do not need to switch everything off; the point is to understand each setting and decide deliberately.

q: Anita uses one long chat for her daughter's science project and her shop's GST questions. What should she do instead?
options: Upgrade to a paid plan so the chat can hold more topics
Delete her chat history after every single question
Switch to a different assistant for each new question
Start a new chat for each new topic
explain: Mixing unrelated topics in one chat confuses the AI, so a fresh chat per topic gives better answers.

q: Which extra line turns a 'summarise this notice' prompt into a practical action list?
options: Use simple words that a child could understand
Tell me if there is anything I need to do, and by when
Make the summary as long and detailed as possible
Translate the summary into three different languages
explain: Asking what you need to do and by when converts a plain summary into concrete action items.

q: Suresh gets a first draft that is too formal for a message to his friend. What is the best next step?
options: Reply in the same chat: that is too formal, I am writing to a friend
Close the chat and accept that AI cannot write casual messages
Copy the formal draft and send it anyway to save time
Start over with a different assistant and the same prompt
explain: Follow-up requests in the same chat quickly refine an answer; two or three usually turn a decent draft into a great one.

q: An AI explains how a mutual fund SIP works. What should you do before making a money decision based on it?
options: Ask the same AI the question again to be fully sure
Trust it, since explanations of basics are never wrong
Confirm with a qualified person or official source
Ask it to explain more simply until it feels right
explain: For money, health or legal matters, use AI to understand basics, then confirm with a qualified person or official source.

q: In the Role, Task, Context, Format formula, which part do beginners skip most often?
options: Role
Context
Task
Format
explain: Context, such as audience, background and constraints, is the most commonly skipped part and often makes the biggest difference.

q: Meena writes: 'Give a 30-second answer I can say aloud, plus 2 delivery tips.' Which part of the formula is this?
options: Role
Task
Context
Format
explain: Format describes how the answer should look, including length, structure and style.

q: You are unsure what background details the AI needs for your resume request. What does the course suggest?
options: Paste your entire resume, including phone and address
Keep the prompt short and accept whatever it produces
Give it a role only and let it guess everything else
Add: before you answer, ask me any questions you need
explain: Asking the AI to interview you first draws out the context it needs, leading to a much better final answer.

q: A Chennai CA firm assistant wants help rewording a client notice reply. What is the safe approach?
options: Replace the client's name, PAN and GSTIN with placeholders first
Paste the full notice, since AI chats are private by default
Paste it only if chat history is switched on in settings
Avoid AI entirely because notices can never be shared
explain: Anonymising with placeholders lets you get help with the wording, then you put the real details back afterwards.

q: Which AI answer is most likely to contain a hallucination?
options: A friendlier rewrite of your own WhatsApp message
Ten caption ideas for a bakery's Diwali hampers
A precise statistic with a court judgment you cannot find
A day-by-day table based on activities you listed
explain: Hallucinations are most common with specific numbers and named sources, especially ones you cannot verify when you search.

q: You ask ChatGPT and Gemini the same tax question and they disagree. How should you treat this?
options: As a red flag to verify the answer on the official portal
As proof that the longer, more detailed answer is correct
As normal, so pick whichever answer sounds more confident
As a sign that both assistants need a paid upgrade
explain: Agreement is not proof, but disagreement is a red flag that tells you to check an official source.

q: According to the course, what makes people actually benefit from AI over time?
options: One long weekend session learning every feature
Short, regular daily practice on real tasks
Waiting until a paid plan offers newer models
Using AI only when a task feels too hard to do
explain: Small, regular practice beats one long session; the 7-day plan uses 10-15 minutes a day on real tasks.

q: Deepak wants his new AI habit to stick. Which tip from the course fits best?
options: Use only English so the answers are always accurate
Avoid saving prompts so you practise writing fresh ones
Skip fact-checking once you are comfortable with AI
Attach it to something he already does, like morning chai
explain: Linking AI use to an existing routine, such as morning chai or checking email, makes the habit easier to keep.
